props.title: Ravenous
props.initialSlug: Starving soldiers turn cannibal in the frontier west

sections.content: Ravenous stands as one of horror cinema's most distinctive cannibal tales, blending pitch-black comedy with frontier dread. Director Antonia Bird crafts a savage critique of Manifest Destiny through the lens of the Wendigo myth and real-life Donner Party horrors. The film shares DNA with other historical horror hybrids like The Company of Wolves (1984) and Brotherhood of the Wolf (2001), using period settings to explore primal fears. Guy Pearce and Robert Carlyle deliver career-defining performances as soldiers grappling with cannibalistic urges in an isolated Fort Spencer.

sections.content: Michael Nyman and Damon Albarn's experimental score deserves special recognition, mixing period instruments with discordant modern elements that perfectly capture the film's unhinged energy. This innovative approach to horror scoring influenced later genre-benders like The VVitch (2015) and Midsommar (2019), where traditional folk elements create unsettling atmosphere. The film's themes of consumption and power connect to other military horror classics like Jacob's Ladder (1990) and The Keep (1983).

The film's exploration of cannibalism as metaphor for American expansionism creates fascinating parallels with other frontier horror films. Like Dead Man (1995) and Ginger Snaps Back: The Beginning (2004), Ravenous uses period authenticity to ground its supernatural elements. The isolated fort setting echoes The Thing (1982), while its dark humor recalls An American Werewolf in London (1981). SUBHEAD: The Military Horror Connection

sections.content: Ravenous sits within a fascinating subgenre of military horror that includes films like Overlord (2018) and Dog Soldiers (2002). These films use military settings to explore how discipline and duty crack under supernatural pressure. The film's critique of manifest destiny and American imperialism finds modern echoes in films like Apocalypse Now Redux (2001) and Predator (1987), where military might confronts primal forces.
